title: FRAME: separating sampling variation from representational cause in medical imaging fairness
abstract: arXiv:2608.25981v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Subgroup performance differences are the standard evidence for fairness bias in medical imaging, and the usual response removes the demographic information that a model encodes. Here we introduce Fair-model Reference And Mechanism Evaluation (FRAME), a two-step framework for auditing such a claim. The first step derives a fair-model reference, the distribution of the difference under exact fairness at the observed subgroup sizes. In the second step, we test the remainder with two operators in representation space. One operator cannot change a within-group ranking by construction. Across 702,206 images and 36 encoders, the reference accounts for a median 41% of the reported race difference and 22% of the age difference. Injecting demographic decodability leaves the remainder unchanged, while entangling the group with the disease direction raises the race difference from 0.077 to 0.118. translated_title: FRAME：在医学影像公平性中将抽样变异与表征原因分离
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25981v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：亚组性能差异是医学影像中公平性偏见的标准证据，通常的应对措施是移除模型编码的人口统计信息。在此，我们引入了公平模型参考与机制评估（FRAME），这是一个用于审计此类声明的两步框架。第一步推导出公平模型参考，即在观察到的亚组规模下，在完全公平条件下的差异分布。第二步，我们在表征空间中使用两个算子检验余项。一个算子通过构造无法改变组内排名。在702,206张图像和36个编码器中，该参考平均解释了报告种族差异的41%和年龄差异的22%。注入人口统计可解码性使余项保持不变，而将群体与疾病方向纠缠会将种族差异从0.077提高到0.118。我们测试的任何干预措施都未显著改变余项。
tldr: 本文提出FRAME框架，通过两步法分离抽样变异与表征原因，发现公平性差异中相当部分可归因于抽样参考，而表征干预对余项影响有限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces FRAME, a two-step framework separating sampling variation from representational causes, revealing that a substantial portion of fairness differences is attributable to sampling reference, while representational interventions have limited impact on the remainder.
